adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: CryptoIntegration.java (~55-70) — behavior change from fail-fast (IllegalStateException on multiple providers) to silent provider selection by order(); ties at order 200 among DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider resolve nondeterministically, possibly running non-FIPS crypto in FIPS deployments

P2: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java (~92-140) — incomplete provider can be selected standalone; UnsupportedOperationException methods (getAlgorithmProvider, getSignature, getAesCbcCipher, getPemUtils) cause runtime crashes instead of failing at selection time

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new ServiceLoader-registered `CryptoProvider` for authz-client (`META-INF/services/...CryptoProvider` -> `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`) and makes `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` call `CryptoIntegration.init(...)`, which will select a provider at runtime. `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` implements `CryptoProvider` but most methods throw `UnsupportedOperationException` (e.g., `getAlgorithmProvider`, `getPemUtils`, `getSignature`, `getAesCbcCipher`, etc.). With the updated `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` logic, if authz-client is used standalone (i.e., this is the only `CryptoProvider` visible to the classloader), it will be selected and those calls would crash at runtime rather than being rejected during selection. The diff doesn’t prove those unsupported methods are actually invoked in authz-client flows, so it’s a concrete robustness/architecture concern rather than a guaranteed functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P2: CryptoProvider.java — adding a new order() method to the public SPI interface breaks compilation of third-party CryptoProvider implementations and fails ServiceLoader instantiation at runtime

P3: ASN1Decoder.java (~56-64, readSequence) — silent truncation of malformed sequences: negative length exits the loop without error, returning corrupt/truncated sequences as successfully parsed; should validate length == 0 after the loop

adjudication.rationale: In `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()`, `length` comes from `readLength()`, which can return `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (`0x80`). The loop condition `while (length > 0)` will then skip parsing entirely and return an empty list without error. Also, when parsing definite-length sequences, the code decrements `length` by `bytes.length` but never validates that it ends exactly at `0`; if a malformed element causes `bytes.length` to exceed the remaining `length`, the method exits with `length < 0` and still returns a partially/over-read result. This matches the finding’s “silent truncation/accept malformed sequences” concern and is a real correctness/security parsing defect in the newly added decoder.

adjudication_records.issue_text: P3: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS (integerToBytes, ~150-165) — no validation of decoded integers; negative BigInteger produces two's-complement bytes silently copied into R/S halves, corrupting signatures instead of throwing IOException; sequence total length also unchecked against input

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.asn1derToConcatenatedRS, the DER INTEGERs are parsed via `new BigInteger(bytes)` (signed) and then normalized by `integerToBytes(...)` without any explicit validation that r/s are non-negative and within the expected fixed-length range. A malformed/non-DER encoding could therefore yield negative BigIntegers and be truncated/padded into the fixed R/S halves instead of throwing. Similarly, ASN1Decoder.readSequence() does not verify that the sequence exactly consumes the entire input (trailing bytes after the sequence would be ignored). These are real robustness/validation gaps visible in the diff, but they don’t clearly break the normal expected path where the DER comes from JCA (which should encode r/s as positive with proper DER rules).

adjudication_records.issue_text: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80) from untrusted DER input; in readNext() the negative length causes new byte[negative] → NegativeArraySizeException (DoS)

adjudication.rationale: In ASN1Decoder.readLength(), an indefinite-length marker (0x80) returns -1. However, in readNext() that value is immediately adjusted by `length += reset()`, where `reset()` returns the number of bytes already read since `mark()` (at least the tag byte + length byte, so >= 2). Thus `length` cannot remain negative and will not cause `new byte[negative]` inside `read(int length)`. Also, readSequence() uses `while (length > 0)`, so a raw -1 length would skip the loop rather than call readNext().

adjudication_records.issue_text: In readSequence(), indefinite-length sequences are silently skipped (length > 0 check) returning an empty list, causing mis-parsing of indefinite-length SEQUENCE wrapping two elements

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()`, the loop condition is `while (length > 0)`. But `readLength()` explicitly returns `-1` for indefinite-length encoding (`length == 0x80`). That means an indefinite-length SEQUENCE will not be parsed at all and `readSequence()` will return an empty `List<byte[]>` without error, i.e., silent mis-parsing. This behavior is directly implied by the diff (`readLength()` returning `-1` and `readSequence()` not handling it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/no-op encoder invocations in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger/sBigInteger) create throwaway encoders and discard results — leftover debugging code

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider#getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` instantiate new ASN1Encoder objects, write into their internal ByteArrayOutputStream, and then discard them without using `toByteArray()` or otherwise consuming the result. The actual returned value is built by a separate `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger))`. Therefore those two standalone encoder invocations are dead/no-op and should be removed, but this is not a functional defect (just redundant code/overhead).

adjudication_records.issue_text: integerToBytes silently truncates over-length r/s integers instead of rejecting malformed input with IOException, and mishandles sign-prefixed arrays from negative BigInteger.toByteArray()

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.ECDSACryptoProvider#asn1derToConcatenatedRS, integerToBytes(BigInteger s, int qLength) uses s.toByteArray() and, when bytes.length > qLength, it silently truncates the most significant bytes (System.arraycopy(bytes, bytes.length - tmp.length, ...)). This will drop not only the valid leading 0x00 used to keep a positive DER INTEGER, but also any other over-length/malformed encoding (including negative values where BigInteger.toByteArray() is sign-prefixed, e.g., leading 0xFF). The code does not validate that the DER INTEGER is non-negative or that the only extra byte is an allowed 0x00 padding, so malformed r/s values can be accepted and altered rather than rejected (no IOException thrown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: detectProvider now silently selects a provider (debug log only) instead of throwing IllegalStateException when multiple CryptoProviders are on the classpath, masking packaging mistakes

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: it now sorts ServiceLoader results by CryptoProvider::order (descending) and always returns the first provider, even when multiple are present. The previous behavior threw IllegalStateException when foundProviders.size() > 1; that exception was removed and replaced with a debug log of “Ignored crypto providers”. This does indeed make multiple-provider presence non-fatal and only visible at debug level, which can mask classpath/packaging mistakes unless the ordering is intentionally relied upon.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider() allocates a KeyStore on every invocation just to fetch its Provider; should be cached in a static/final field (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java:53-59)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getBouncyCastleProvider(), the method calls `KeyStore.getInstance(KeyStore.getDefaultType())` on every invocation solely to access `.getProvider()` (see AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java). This repeatedly constructs a KeyStore instance and may be unnecessarily expensive; caching the Provider (e.g., in a static/final field) would avoid repeated allocations. This is a performance/efficiency concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.init(...) is invoked on every AuthzClient.create(...), potentially triggering a repeated ServiceLoader classpath scan if init is not idempotent (AuthzClient.java:95)

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` now unconditionally calls `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())`, so it will be invoked on every `AuthzClient.create(...)` call. However, the diff does not show whether `CryptoIntegration.init(...)` is idempotent/cached; only `detectProvider(...)` is shown and it uses `ServiceLoader.load(...)` (classpath scan) when invoked. This makes the review comment a valid, diff-grounded performance/architecture concern, but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: readLength() returns -1 for indefinite-length (0x80) input, and neither readSequence nor readNext handles -1, causing read(-1) to throw an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException instead of the declared IOException on malformed DER input

adjudication.rationale: In the new ASN1Decoder, readLength() explicitly returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). That return value is not validated by callers. In particular, readInteger() does `int length = readLength(); byte[] bytes = read(length);` so an input like INTEGER + 0x80 will call read(-1), which allocates `new byte[-1]` and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException rather than an IOException. While readSequence() won’t call read(-1) directly (it just skips the loop when length == -1), it also doesn’t reject indefinite length, so behavior on malformed/BER input is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: readSequence() allows length to go negative when a decoded element exceeds the declared sequence length, exiting the while loop silently and accepting truncated/corrupt structures as valid, potentially yielding garbage R/S values

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `ASN1Decoder.readSequence()`, the loop decrements the declared SEQUENCE length by each returned element’s total encoded size (`length = length - bytes.length`) but never validates that the final length is exactly 0 or that it didn’t go negative. If `readNext()` returns an element larger than the remaining declared `length`, `length` becomes negative and the `while (length > 0)` loop exits without throwing, returning a list as if parsing succeeded. This is directly visible in `ASN1Decoder` and can lead `asn1derToConcatenatedRS(...)` to accept malformed/truncated/corrupt DER and produce incorrect R/S values.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider() silently ignores multiple crypto providers by selecting via order() with only debug-level logging, masking deployment misconfigurations (e.g., FIPS + default provider present) instead of failing fast
AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported yet.') in ~20 interface methods, causing deferred, uninformative runtime failures if the provider wins order() selection

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` registered via `META-INF/services/org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider`, and `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())`, meaning this provider can be selected at runtime. In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, many `CryptoProvider` methods (`getAlgorithmProvider`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getPemUtils`, `getSignature`, etc.) throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`, so any code path that uses `CryptoIntegration.getProvider()` for those operations will now fail at runtime with an unhelpful exception. The finding’s “if the provider wins order() selection” is somewhat imprecise (it returns `order() = 100` while other providers in the diff return `200`), but it can still be the chosen provider when it’s the only one on that classloader, and the incomplete implementation is a concrete, diff-grounded risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getKeyStore() uses KeyStore.getInstance(format.name()) with the default provider instead of passing BouncyIntegration.PROVIDER like other providers, potentially failing or behaving differently for BCFKS format

Round-trip test in ECDSAAlgorithmTest only proves self-consistency; no comparison against known-good DER signature or server-side ECDSACryptoProvider output, so compatibility with server verification is untested

adjudication.rationale: In `authz/client/src/test/java/.../ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java`, the test signs with `Signature` to obtain a DER signature (`byte[] sign = signature.sign()`), then uses the *same* `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` implementation to convert DER -> concatenated RS -> DER -> concatenated RS and only asserts `rsConcat` equals `rsConcat2`. It does not assert the regenerated DER (`asn1Des`) matches the original DER (`sign`), nor does it compare outputs against any known-good vectors or another implementation (e.g., server-side provider). So the finding that the test mainly proves self-consistency and doesn’t directly test cross-compatibility is supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: concatenatedRSToASN1DER in AuthzClientCryptoProvider contains dead encoding calls (two ASN1Encoder instances created, written to, and discarded), which no round-trip test can detect

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.ECDSACryptoProvider#concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` each create a new ASN1Encoder, write to it, and then discard it without using the result. The returned DER encoding is produced by a separate encoder instance in the subsequent `return ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(...)...` block, so those two calls are dead/unobservable. This is a real, diff-grounded issue (wasted work / likely leftover code), but it does not change behavior, so it’s not a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Behavior change in CryptoIntegration.detectProvider from throwing IllegalStateException on multiple providers to silently preferring highest order() has no unit test covering provider ordering or downgrade-from-error scenario

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` to sort providers by the new `CryptoProvider.order()` (descending) and no longer throws when `foundProviders.size() > 1`; it now selects the first and only logs the rest as ignored (`common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java`). While `order()` is added to `CryptoProvider` and implemented in several providers, the only new test added (`authz/client/src/test/.../ECDSAAlgorithmTest.java`) covers ECDSA signature conversion and does not exercise `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` behavior (ordering selection or the prior error-on-multiple-providers scenario). This is a specific missing-test gap for newly introduced selection logic, not a directly verifiable runtime defect in the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No edge-case tests for ASN1Decoder: high-tag-number form, indefinite length causing likely infinite loop in readSequence on malformed input, negative/out-of-bounds lengths; missing fuzz-style negative tests for truncated/corrupt DER

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces nontrivial DER parsing logic in `ASN1Decoder` (`readTagNumber`, `readLength`, `readSequence`, `readNext`) but adds only a positive-path test `ECDSAAlgorithmTest` that exercises valid ECDSA signatures, not malformed/truncated/corrupt DER inputs. There are no tests covering edge cases like high-tag-number encoding (`readTagNumber` branch when `tagNo == 0x1f`) or error paths in `readLength` (e.g., oversized lengths, EOF). Note: the finding’s claim about an “infinite loop” on indefinite length is not supported by the code as written (`readLength()` returns `-1`, and `readSequence()` loops only while `length > 0`), but the broader point about missing negative/edge-case tests for the new decoder is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration test that AuthzClient.create() initializes the crypto provider by asserting CryptoIntegration.getProvider() is non-null/AuthzClientCryptoProvider

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new behavior in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` by calling `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` before constructing the client. The only added test (`ECDSAAlgorithmTest`) validates ECDSA signature format conversions via `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, but there is no test that exercises `AuthzClient.create()` and asserts `CryptoIntegration.getProvider()` is initialized (e.g., non-null or that the selected provider is `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` when used from the authz-client module). This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test concern for newly added initialization logic, not a proven runtime bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead/duplicated code in concatenatedRSToASN1DER: two ASN1Encoder.create().write() statements discard results, only the writeDerSeq chain is returned (AuthzClientCryptoProvider.java ~101-103)

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the two statements `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create new encoders and write into them, but the results are not stored or used. The method then returns a separately-created encoder via `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger))...`. This is verifiable dead/duplicated work in the diff, but it does not affect correctness since the returned value comes from the later chain.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration now silently picks highest-order provider instead of throwing on multiple providers; ties at order 200 (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, FIPS1402Provider) make selection nondeterministic (CryptoIntegration.java ~57-70)

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider to sort loaded CryptoProvider instances by `order()` descending and then return `foundProviders.get(0)` even when multiple providers are present (it no longer throws). In this same diff, DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all implement `order()` returning 200. With equal sort keys, the comparator yields 0 and the selected provider depends on the underlying ServiceLoader iteration order, so which provider becomes index 0 is not explicitly defined by this code and can vary with classpath/service ordering. This makes provider selection ambiguous/nondeterministic under ties, whereas previously multiple providers would have been rejected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClient.create() mutates global static crypto state via CryptoIntegration.init, potentially replacing the global provider in multi-classloader environments; also CryptoIntegration stays uninitialized if AuthzClient.create() is never called (AuthzClient.java:95)

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a global side-effect in `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` by calling `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` before constructing the client. `CryptoIntegration` is a shared integration point (static access via `CryptoIntegration.getProvider()` and provider auto-detection via `ServiceLoader`), so initializing it from a library factory method can couple `AuthzClient` creation to global crypto-provider selection and potentially interfere with other components/classloaders that expect to control when/which provider is initialized. However, the claim that crypto "stays uninitialized if AuthzClient.create() is never called" is not verifiable from this diff, and whether init actually "replaces" an existing provider depends on `CryptoIntegration.init` implementation not shown here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider throws UnsupportedOperationException for ~15 of 19 CryptoProvider methods, risking runtime failures on calls like getPemUtils() or getAlgorithmProvider()

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new service-loaded `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (`META-INF/services/...CryptoProvider`) and `AuthzClient.create(...)` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init(...)`, meaning this provider can become the active `CryptoProvider` when no higher-`order()` provider is on the classpath. In `AuthzClientCryptoProvider`, most `CryptoProvider` methods (`getAlgorithmProvider`, `getPemUtils`, `getCertificateUtils`, `getSignature`, etc.) explicitly `throw new UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")`, so any runtime path that uses those APIs via `CryptoIntegration.getProvider()` would fail. The diff does not show any such call sites, so this is a real, diff-grounded robustness/architecture concern rather than a provable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder readSequence mishandles indefinite-length BER: readLength returns -1 and the while loop runs until a confusing EOFException instead of a clear 'indefinite length not supported' error (ASN1Decoder.java ~55-70)
matched_golden_ids: When length starts at -1 from indefinite-length encoding, the arithmetic 'length = length - bytes.length' will behave unexpectedly, potentially leading to incorrect processing of encoded data.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point to the same core problem: indefinite-length BER yields a length of -1, but the decoder proceeds as if it were a definite length. This causes the length/loop accounting to behave incorrectly (e.g., subtracting bytes from -1 or looping until EOF), leading to improper processing rather than explicitly rejecting/handling indefinite lengths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: CryptoIntegration.detectProvider: replacing fail-fast IllegalStateException for multiple providers with silent debug-log + order-based preference allows non-FIPS crypto to silently replace FIPS crypto when both providers are on the classpath — security/compliance regression and silent-pass guard removal

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes CryptoIntegration.detectProvider from fail-fast on multiple CryptoProvider implementations to selecting one after sorting by CryptoProvider::order and only debug-logging the rest (common/.../CryptoIntegration.java). This removes the previous guard against ambiguous provider selection. Additionally, DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider, and FIPS1402Provider all return the same order value (200), so when more than one is present the chosen provider can depend on ServiceLoader iteration order (not guaranteed), meaning a non-FIPS provider could be selected even if the FIPS provider is on the classpath, with no exception raised.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.integerToBytes (via asn1derToConcatenatedRS ~L180): if DER-encoded r or s is longer than len bytes, it silently truncates to the last qLength bytes instead of failing, so corrupted/hostile signatures decode into wrong-but-valid-length signatures; negative r/s values also round-trip silently

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().asn1derToConcatenatedRS, r and s are parsed as signed integers (ASN1Decoder.readInteger uses `new BigInteger(bytes)`), but ECDSA r/s must be non-negative. Then `integerToBytes(BigInteger s, int qLength)` will (a) silently truncate when `bytes.length > qLength` by taking the last qLength bytes, and (b) does not reject negative values. This matches the finding: malformed/hostile DER INTEGER encodings (extra leading bytes or sign-related encodings) can be mapped into a fixed-length output without failing, producing a different-but-valid-length concatenated signature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClient.java:95: CryptoIntegration.init() runs on every AuthzClient.create() call and detectProvider is not synchronized, so concurrent create() calls race on the static provider field and the winning provider is nondeterministic when multiple providers exist

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AuthzClient.create(Configuration)` now calls `CryptoIntegration.init(AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader())` on every create (AuthzClient.java), and `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` is a plain static method with no synchronization added. However, the finding’s claim of a concrete race on a "static provider field" and nondeterministic winner cannot be verified from this diff alone because the `init()` implementation and any static state it mutates are not shown. What is verifiable is a new repeated initialization call-site and the lack of explicit thread-safety in the shown provider-detection logic, which is a legitimate design/thread-safety concern but not a provable defect from the provided changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider: nearly every method throws UnsupportedOperationException('Not supported yet.'); with order()=100 it can be selected when no other provider is present, causing opaque runtime UOE failures instead of the previous clear 'no crypto provider found' error — a late-failure trap

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a ServiceLoader-registered `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (META-INF/services/...) and forces `CryptoIntegration.init(...)` in `AuthzClient.create(...)`. `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider(...)` now always selects the highest `order()` provider rather than failing on multiples. In an authz-client-only classpath, the only provider may be `AuthzClientCryptoProvider` (order=100), but most `CryptoProvider` methods in it throw `UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet.")` (e.g., `getSignature`, `getKeyFactory`, `getX509CertFactory`, etc.). This can shift failure from an early clear "no cryptoProvider" error to later runtime UOE if code paths call those methods, which is a concrete, diff-grounded completeness/robustness concern, even if the authz-client currently only needs the ECDSA conversion methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ASN1Decoder.readSequence(): the loop 'while (length > 0) { length -= readNext().length }' never terminates if readNext() returns a zero-length byte[] (zero-length DER element), causing an infinite loop / DoS on malformed signature input

adjudication.rationale: In the added ASN1Decoder.readSequence(), the loop decrements `length` by `bytes.length` where `bytes` is returned from `readNext()`. But `readNext()` cannot return a zero-length array: it calls `mark()`, then reads at least the tag byte (`readTag()` increments `count`), reads the length, then does `length += reset()`. Even if the DER element has zero content length (`readLength()` returns 0), `reset()` returns the number of bytes consumed for tag/length (>= 2), so `read(length)` will allocate/read a byte[] of size >= 2. Therefore the specific infinite-loop scenario “readNext() returns zero-length byte[]” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding CryptoProvider.order() to the interface is a binary-compatibility break: existing third-party CryptoProvider implementations that don't recompile against the new interface will fail to load via ServiceLoader

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new abstract method `int order()` to the `CryptoProvider` interface (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoProvider.java). `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider()` now unconditionally calls it via `Comparator.comparingInt(CryptoProvider::order).reversed()` when loading providers (common/src/main/java/org/keycloak/common/crypto/CryptoIntegration.java). Any existing third-party `CryptoProvider` implementation compiled against the old interface (without `order()`) may still be discovered by `ServiceLoader`, but will fail at runtime when `order()` is invoked (e.g., `AbstractMethodError`), breaking provider loading. This is a binary-compatibility/runtime behavior break exposed by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: AuthzClientCryptoProvider.concatenatedRSToASN1DER (~L150): creates three ASN1Encoder instances where the first two are dead code (output built only from the third) — dead code that should be cleaned up

adjudication.rationale: In AuthzClientCryptoProvider.getEcdsaCryptoProvider().concatenatedRSToASN1DER, the lines `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` create encoder instances and write into them but their results are not used. The returned value is built only from the later `ASN1Encoder.create().writeDerSeq(ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger), ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger))...`. This is redundant/dead code (unnecessary allocations) but does not change correctness.
